  1. Show HN: TrnRT – An open-source LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium

    • AI
    • Hardware

    54 points · 8 comments · 17 Nov 2026, 16:01 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — TrnRT is an open-source LLM inference engine for AWS Trainium, with NKI megakernels, a claimed 1M-token context capability, and an OpenAI-compatible API. The HN post described early GLM-5.3 Flash support and performance experiments on trn2 hardware.

    Discussion — Readers welcomed more usable Trainium software but questioned benchmarks, metrics, model support, and the maturity of AWS’s ecosystem. The author and commenters discussed throughput reporting and the gap with Nvidia-oriented tooling.

  2. Show HN: Nobody blocks a keyboard – Rooted Android as a physical USB Deck

    • Hardware
    • Security

    56 points · 57 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 14:18 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Emittr turns a rooted Android phone into a USB HID keyboard and mouse using the Linux USB gadget subsystem, intended for controlled or locked-down systems where host software cannot be installed. The author says it exposes a LAN web UI and does not store credentials on the rooted phone.

    Discussion — The thread concentrated on security and misuse: commenters compared it with BadUSB, questioned using it with air-gapped systems, and noted platforms and tools that block untrusted USB devices. Others suggested KVM-like extensions and alternatives.

  3. What's Next for Nvidia?

    • AI
    • Economics
    • Hardware

    485 points · 588 comments · 15 Nov 2026, 23:55 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Steve Blank argues that Jensen Huang’s reported departure leaves Nvidia exposed to a founder-to-executor transition. He credits Huang with CUDA, the deep-learning pivot, and integrated AI datacenter systems, and says the board needs a successor able to operate today’s business while repeatedly remaking it as hyperscalers develop their own chips.

    Discussion — Discussion both extended and challenged the founder-versus-executor framing. Commenters debated whether Nvidia should cannibalize its GPU business before rivals do, how custom chips and weaker CUDA lock-in could affect margins, and whether Apple and Microsoft are fair post-founder cautionary examples; unverified speculation about the departure was explicitly contested.

  4. Show HN: Fursoy – Out-of-order RV64IMAFDV core in SystemVerilog (Linux 6.6)

    • Hardware

    86 points · 39 comments · 14 Nov 2026, 14:06 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Fursoy Slice-1 is a 64-bit out-of-order superscalar RISC-V processor in SystemVerilog that boots Linux 6.6.50 and BusyBox under Sv39. The repository documents 2-wide execution, verification work, and pre-layout 500 MHz Nangate 45 nm timing closure.

    Discussion — Readers debated what AI assistance changes in CPU design and whether simulation and synthesis demonstrate real hardware quality. A detailed technical exchange covered verification, timing, microarchitecture documentation, FPGA plans, and remaining rough edges.

    • Economics

    1114 points · 651 comments · 14 Nov 2026, 02:52 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — TechPowerUp reported allegations that Nvidia reinforced GPU scarcity by funding AI startups that then bought Nvidia GPUs. The article framed the account as an allegation about incentives and market structure, not an established finding.
